- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often lags the true decline.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift downward too slowly, failing to capture rapid downward corrections.
- In periods of high volatility, model underreacts to true price drops — especially when true prices fall below 65.
- Model exhibits “lagged” behavior: true price drops often occur before model adjusts, suggesting delayed sensitivity to recent data.
- When true prices are below 60, model tends to forecast higher than actual — indicating underweighting of low-price signals.
- Model overfits to recent high prices, failing to recognize that price peaks are often followed by sharp corrections.
- In low-volatility periods, model forecasts remain flat or slightly upward, missing true mean-reversion to prior levels.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price drops in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window.
